title: Playing for strangers
summary: Play a short set of about two minutes for people who are not family, or a gathering standing in for it.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil
a place to play for people who are not family, or a family gathering standing in for it

figure.alt: Three boxes stacked, one for each of up to three short pieces that add up to about two minutes, the set played cold with no warm-up before the first note.

steps.title: Playing for strangers
steps.body:
A family recital is kind. A stranger's ear is not unkind, just busy, and it will not wait for you to settle in. Playing for people who did not come specifically to hear you is its own kind of practice. This week is built around getting a taste of it.

1. Choose two or three short pieces that add up to about two minutes.
2. Practise starting cold, straight from silence, with no warm-up before the first note, since a stranger will not give you one.
3. Play the full set once at home exactly as you would in public, and time it with the phone.
4. If a real audience of strangers is not possible this week, play the set for a family gathering instead. Treat it exactly the same way: no do-overs, no explaining a slip.

Playing for people who owe you nothing is where performing stops being only for family, and starts being a skill you actually own.

figure.alt: The same three boxes, the set run again each sitting, starting cold every time, since a stranger's ear will not wait for a warm-up.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: choose the two or three pieces, time a cold run-through
Sitting 2: run the set again, starting cold, no warm-up
Sitting 3: run the set a third time, in a different room if possible
Sitting 4: the real set, for strangers or a family gathering standing in for it
An old piece added to the set if there is time to spare

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Record the full set in one take, starting cold, no warm-up before the first note, hands in the frame.
